answer: Cap identity supply, not its price. Each epoch mints a fixed number of active seats, drawn at random from applicants that re-stake. Seats are non-transferable and single-tenant, so cloning a thousand keys only fills a queue whose length never grows: as the tide of applicants rises, the draw gets crowded, not weightier. Cohorts enter on a terrace of staggered epochs, so no operator sweeps a round. If new holders share one funding source, the draw repeats. A hard zenith on seats per entity makes a sybil farm buy the whole capacity: cost linear, payoff flat.
